A boat heads due north at 10 mph across a river whose current flows due west at 6 mph. What is the direction of travel, in degrees counterclockwise from east, from 0 to 360, to 1 decimal place?

problems.text: resultant direction: 10 at 90; 6 at 180 to 1 dp
problems.explain: Break each into components: 10 at 90° is ⟨10 cos 90°, 10 sin 90°⟩ ≈ ⟨0, 10⟩; 6 at 180° is ⟨6 cos 180°, 6 sin 180°⟩ ≈ ⟨−6, 0⟩. Adding, the resultant is about ⟨−6, 10⟩. Its reference angle is tan⁻¹(10/6) ≈ 59.0362°; the resultant points into quadrant II, so θ = 180° − 59.0362° ≈ 120.9638°. So it is 121.0°.

problems.explain: Break each into components: 80 at 210° is ⟨80 cos 210°, 80 sin 210°⟩ ≈ ⟨−69.28, −40⟩; 15 at 80° is ⟨15 cos 80°, 15 sin 80°⟩ ≈ ⟨2.604, 14.772⟩. Adding, the resultant is about ⟨−66.676, −25.228⟩. Its length is √((−66.676)² + (−25.228)²) ≈ 71.2891. So it is 71.3 N.
